rtf_document(font_lang = "ja") stops: "`font_lang` must be a named character vector of languages per font slot, e.g. c(east_asian = "ja")."; an unknown language stops: "`font_lang`: unknown language(s) "jp"; use ..."; a slot name that is not distinct among latin / east_asian / complex stops: "`font_lang`: names must be distinct slots among latin, east_asian, complex."
rtf_document(file = "output/t_dm.rtf") names the RTF file the document is written to, which generate_rtfreport(doc) writes when it is given no file_path; NULL (the default) names none.
rtf_document(file = ) with a vector, an empty string, NA or a number stops: "`file` must be a single string: the RTF file's path."

A watermark given in rtf_document(watermark = ) is the document's; a section's rtf_section(secinfo = list(watermark = )) overrides it for that section, and watermark = NA switches it off for that section alone.

The program named for the run tokens is, in order: generate_rtfreport(program = ), rtf_document(program = ), options(rtfreporter.program), the program found (the file source() runs, the script Rscript runs, knitr's document, RStudio's editor), then generate_rtfreport(program_fallback = ) or rtf_document(program_fallback = ); a program said is not announced, one found or fallen back to is said in a message.

A file given in rtf_document(file = ) is written when generate_rtfreport() is given no file_path; a file_path given to generate_rtfreport() wins; and with overwrite = FALSE the document's file that exists stops the call.
A default argument of rtf_document() (font_table, page, font_lang) is taken from the rtfreporter.* option when the argument is not given; an explicit argument beats the option.
Tokens of one's own set in options(rtfreporter.tokens = ) and in rtf_document(tokens = ) are both filled; for the same name the document's value wins.
rtf_config() returns a modified copy of the rtf_document and leaves the original unchanged, so variants of one composed report are independent.
rtf_config() leaves the document's contents and sections identical to the original's.
An argument of rtf_config() that is NULL (the default) changes nothing; only the arguments passed are changed.
rtf_config(font_table = ) replaces the document's font table as a whole.
rtf_config(color_table = ) replaces the document's colour table as a whole.
rtf_config(page = ) takes an rtf_page() or a named list and is merged per key onto the current page: passing width_in and height_in changes those two keys and keeps the orientation and margins.
rtf_config(default_format = ) takes an rtf_default_format() or a named list and is merged per key onto the current default format.
rtf_config(watermark = ) takes an rtf_watermark(), a bare string, or NA to remove the document's watermark; NULL (the default) leaves it unchanged, so NA, not NULL, clears one.
rtf_config(font_lang = ) replaces the document's font language; NA removes it; NULL (the default) leaves it unchanged.
rtf_config(<not an rtf_document>) stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document object".

rtf_config(page = "a4") stops: "`page` must be an rtf_page() object or a named list of its settings (e.g. list(paper_size = "A4")), not the string "a4".  For a paper size write page = rtf_page(paper_size = "a4")."
rtf_config(watermark = list(1, 2)) stops: "`watermark` must be an rtf_watermark object, a single string, or NULL / NA for none."

rtf_config(font_lang = "ja") stops with the font_lang messages of rtf_document(): "`font_lang` must be a named character vector of languages per font slot, e.g. c(east_asian = "ja")."; likewise an unknown language or slot.
rtf_config(page = ) and rtf_config(default_format = ) merge per key onto what rtf_document() set, while font_table, color_table, watermark and font_lang replace it whole.

rtf_default_format() returns an object of class rtf_default_format whose fields are font_size_half_points, row_height_twips, cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips, markup, title_format, footnote_format, title_width and footnote_width; with no argument they equal the factory baseline.
rtf_default_format(font_size_half_points = 18L) is the body font size in half-points (18 is 9 pt); an argument not passed falls back to options(rtfreporter.font_size_half_points).
rtf_default_format(font_size_half_points = 0) (or NA, or a vector) stops: "`font_size_half_points` must be a single positive integer."

rtf_default_format(row_height_twips = ) is the default row height in twips for every table-shaped element (content table, page header and footer, title and footnote); NULL (the default) keeps the font-aware baseline.

rtf_default_format(cell_padding_left_twips = , cell_padding_right_twips = ) are the default cell padding in twips, border to text; NULL (the default) keeps the baseline of 0; an explicit 0 is honoured.
rtf_default_format(row_height_twips = -1) (also for the two padding arguments; or NA, or a vector) stops: "`row_height_twips` must be a single non-negative integer (twips) or NULL."
rtf_default_format(markup = "script") is the default cell-text markup: "script" (^{} / _{} super- and subscript), "relational" (>= and <= to the symbols), "all" (both) or "none".
rtf_default_format(markup = "bogus") stops: "`markup` must be a subset of c("script", "relational") (or "all" / "none" / NULL); got: bogus".
rtf_default_format(title_format = "text") renders the page title as plain centred paragraphs; "table" renders it as a content-width single-column table.
rtf_default_format(footnote_format = "table") renders the footnote as a content-width table with the separator; "text" renders it as plain paragraphs.
rtf_default_format(title_format = "fancy") (or footnote_format) stops: "`title_format` / `footnote_format` must be "text" or "table"; got 'fancy'."

rtf_default_format(title_width = , footnote_width = ) is the width of the title or footnote block: "content" (follow the table body), "page" (the writable width), a fraction in (0, 1] of the writable width, or twips; NULL keeps the default; it applies to the "table" form.
rtf_default_format(footnote_width = "wide") (or title_width = -1) stops: "`footnote_width` must be "content", "page", a fraction in (0, 1], or twips."
A per-module setting (rtftable(row_height_twips = ), rtftable(cell_padding_left_twips = ), rtf_header, rtf_footer, rtf_table_style) overrides the document default from rtf_default_format().

An argument of rtf_default_format() that is not passed falls back to its rtfreporter.* option (font_size_half_points, markup, title_format, footnote_format, title_width, footnote_width); an explicit argument beats the option.

A footnote row given as c(l = , c = , r = ) needs footnote_format = "table"; under footnote_format = "text" it stops: "A c(l = , c = , r = ) footnote row needs the table form. Set footnote_format = "table" (the default), or give the row as a single string."

rtf_page() returns an object of class rtf_page; with no argument it is landscape Letter with 0.75 inch margins and no explicit width, height or header / footer distance, equal to the factory baseline.
rtf_page(paper_size = "letter") names a preset (case-insensitive): "letter" (8.5 x 11 in), "legal" (8.5 x 14), "A4" (210 x 297 mm), "A3" or "A5"; the preset is oriented by orientation.
rtf_page(paper_size = c("A4", "letter")) or a number stops: "`paper_size` must be a single preset name (e.g. "A4") or NULL."
A paper_size that is no preset (page = rtf_page(paper_size = "tabloid")) stops when the file is written: "Unknown `paper_size` "tabloid". Known sizes: letter, legal, a4, a3, a5."
rtf_page(orientation = "landscape") is "landscape" (the paper's long side is the width, and \\landscape is written) or "portrait" (no document-level \\landscape).
rtf_page(orientation = "sideways") stops: "`orientation` must be "landscape" or "portrait"."

rtf_page(width_in = , height_in = ) give the page size in inches; they win over paper_size and are used as given, the orientation being inferred (width_in >= height_in is landscape); NULL (the default) uses paper_size.
rtf_page(width_in = "wide") (or height_in, or a value that is zero, negative, NA or a vector) stops: "`width_in` must be a single positive number of inches, or NULL."

A paper_size given with explicit width_in / height_in is ignored with a warning when the file is written: "Both `paper_size` and `width_in`/`height_in` were supplied; the explicit dimensions take precedence and `paper_size` is ignored."
notes: rtf_page() stores the default paper_size, so the warning also fires with dimensions alone (#761)

statement: An orientation that contradicts explicit dimensions warns when the file is written: "`orientation = "landscape"` contradicts the given dimensions (8.27 x 11.69 in, => portrait); using the dimensions as given."; the dimensions are not swapped.
notes: rtf_page() stores the default orientation, so the warning also fires with dimensions alone (#761)

statement: rtf_page(margin_top_in = , margin_bottom_in = , margin_left_in = , margin_right_in = ) are the four page margins in inches, 0.75 by default.
notes: the help details say other margins (#761)

statement: rtf_page(margin_top_in = -1) (or any margin, or header_dist_in / footer_dist_in, that is zero, negative, NA or a vector) stops: "`margin_top_in` must be a single positive number of inches, or NULL."

rtf_page(header_dist_in = , footer_dist_in = ) give the distance of the header or footer band from the page edge in inches; NULL (the default) uses the full top or bottom margin, so the band sits at the margin boundary.
An rtf_page() argument not passed falls back to its rtfreporter.page.* option, an explicit argument beats the option, and the option beats the factory default.
rtf_section(doc, page = 1, header = h, footer = f) stores the section under its page; header = / footer = and the superseded secinfo = list(header = , footer = ) give the same sections.
rtf_section(page = 2) starts a section at page 2; pages are numbered from 1 in the order of the contents.
rtf_section(page = c(1, 3), secinfo = list(list(...), list(...))) starts several sections at once, one per entry of page; the number of sections in secinfo must match the length of page.
rtf_section(page = NULL), the default, stores the section as the "_default" template used by rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) and by pages with no section of their own.

rtf_section(header = h) gives the section's running header, an rtf_header(); NULL (the default) means inherit: a section with no header of its own keeps the previous section's, so only the first section's NULL leaves its pages without one.
rtf_section(footer = f) gives the section's running footer, an rtf_footer(), with the same inheriting NULL as header; rtf_header("") after a section that has a header gives a blank band.
rtf_section(secinfo = ) (superseded, documented, not warned) is a named list list(header = , footer = , watermark = ), or for several sections a list of such lists, one per entry of page.
rtf_section(secinfo = list(watermark = )) takes an rtf_watermark() or a string for that section, and NA to switch off the document's watermark for it.
A header or footer in a section is an rtf_header() / rtf_footer(), its rows (a list) or its text (a string); a string given with a vector page is applied to every page named.
rtf_section(doc, page = 1) with no header, footer or secinfo stores an empty section list(header = NULL, footer = NULL).
rtf_section(<not an rtf_document>) stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document object".
rtf_section(header = h, secinfo = list(header = h)) stops: "Give the section as `header =` / `footer =` or as `secinfo =`, not both."

rtf_section(secinfo = list(hdr = h)) stops: "`secinfo` has `hdr`: a section has `header`, `footer` and `watermark` only (rtf_section(header = , footer = ))."; an unnamed element stops with "has unnamed elements" in the same place.
rtf_section(secinfo = list(header = 1)) stops: "`secinfo`'s `header` must be an rtf_header() or NULL, not a numeric." (and `footer`, rtf_footer()).
rtf_section(page = c(1, 2), secinfo = list(list(header = NULL))) stops: "Length of page (2) must match length of secinfo (1)".
rtf_section(page = c(1, 2), secinfo = "oops") stops: "When page is a vector, secinfo must be a list of section objects".
An explicit rtf_section(page = 1) wins over the first auto section (rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE)); the page after it keeps its own auto section.
combine_sections(A = pages) puts the argument's name on its first page and blanks the names of the remaining pages, so one paginated table is one section.
combine_sections() takes each argument as a list of rtftables (an as_rtftables() result) and returns their pages as one flat list, in the order of the arguments, each argument labelled by its name.
combine_sections() takes a bare rtftable as a one-page section.
An unnamed argument of combine_sections() gets an empty name on its first page, so its pages fall through into the previous section.
combine_sections() with no argument returns list(); an argument that is an empty list is skipped.
combine_sections(A = 42) stops: "Each argument to `combine_sections()` must be an rtftable or a list of rtftables."
combine_sections(A = list(1, 2)) stops: "`combine_sections()` argument 'A' must contain only rtftable objects." (an unnamed argument is named by its position, "#2").

The list from combine_sections() given to rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) makes one section per argument; a section opens where the page name changes, an empty name continues the open section, and a name that comes back after another opens a new one.
rtf_titles(doc, titles) sets the title of every content (table or figure page) already added and returns the modified document; the original is unchanged.
rtf_titles(titles = list(...)) of length equal to the number of contents gives each content its own block; a block that is NULL leaves that content with no title.
rtf_titles(titles = list("Common")), a list of length 1, gives the one block to every content.
rtf_titles(titles = c("Table 14.1.1", "Population")), a character vector, is one block (its lines) for every content.

A title block is a character vector (one entry per row) or a list of rows, a row being a string or a styled list(text =, align =, bold =, italic =, underline =, color =, border =); an empty string is a blank row; rows default to centred and bold.

A page's heading (rtf_tables(auto_title = TRUE), a plan's plan_paginate_group(heading_at = "title")) is not replaced by rtf_titles(): it stays as the block's last row, under the titles given, and once when rtf_titles() is called again.
rtf_titles() replaces the titles whole: the continued line that rtf_tables(cont_title = ) adds to a table's later pages goes with the titles it replaces.
rtf_titles(font_size_half_points = 20L) sets the font size of the block in half-points, overriding the document default from rtf_default_format(); NULL (the default) inherits.

rtf_titles(row_height_twips = ) sets the block's row height; a font size given without a height recomputes the height from that size rather than inheriting one chosen for another size, and an explicit height always wins.
rtf_titles(markup = ) sets the cell-text markup of the block alone ("script", "relational", "all", "none"); NULL (the default) inherits the document's.
rtf_titles(align = ) sets the block's default row alignment ("left", "center", "right"); a row's own align still beats it; NULL (the default) inherits.

rtf_titles(font = "Arial") sets the block's font family; one not in the document's font_table is added to it automatically; a named vector gives one family per script slot (latin, east_asian, complex, optional hansi); NULL (the default) inherits.
rtf_titles(<not an rtf_document>, ...) stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document object".

rtf_titles() before any content is added stops: "Cannot set titles before any content has been added.  Call rtf_titles() after rtf_tables() / rtf_figures(): it sets the titles of the pages already added (one block per page, or one for all).  Or pass `titles =` to rtf_tables() / rtf_figures()."
rtf_titles(d, 1) (neither a list nor a character vector) stops: "`titles` must be a list (one block per page) or a character vector (one block for every page)."
rtf_titles() with a list of 3 blocks for 2 contents stops: "`titles` has 3 blocks but the document has 2 pages: give one block per page, or one block (a list of length 1) for every page."

rtf_titles(font_size_half_points = -1) stops: "`rtf_titles(font_size_half_points)` must be a single positive integer (half-points)."; row_height_twips: "`rtf_titles(row_height_twips)` must be a single non-negative integer (twips) or NULL."; align: "`rtf_titles(align)` must be "left", "center" or "right"."; font: "`rtf_titles(font)` must be a single font family name, or a named vector of them per script slot, ...".
rtf_footnotes(doc, footnotes) sets the footnote of every content (table or figure page) already added and returns the modified document; the original is unchanged.
rtf_footnotes(footnotes = list(...)) of length equal to the number of contents gives each content its own block; a NULL element suppresses the footnote of that content.
rtf_footnotes(footnotes = list("Common")), a list of length 1, gives the one block to every content.
rtf_footnotes(footnotes = "Source: ADSL"), a character vector, is one block (its lines) for every content.

A footnote row is a single string, or a named vector c(l = , c = , r = ) of up to three cells positioned left, centre and right (the model of rtf_footer()); a bare string lands in the slot that align selects (left by default); a row's own slot beats the block align; a blank string is a row of its own.
rtf_footnotes(border = ) is NULL (the default) for no rule; an rtf_border(), e.g. rtf_border(top = TRUE), puts a rule on the first row only.
notes: the help description says a top rule by default (#761)

statement: rtf_footnotes(font_size_half_points = ) sets the font size of the block in half-points, the row height following the size unless row_height_twips is given; NULL (the default) inherits the document's.
rtf_footnotes(row_height_twips = ) sets the block's row height in twips; an explicit height wins over the one the font size implies.
rtf_footnotes(markup = ) sets the cell-text markup of the block alone; markup can be switched on or off for the footnote without touching the document's.
rtf_footnotes(align = ) sets the block's default row alignment (and the slot a bare string lands in); a row's own l / c / r beats it.
rtf_footnotes(font = ) sets the block's font family (one family, or a named vector per script slot); one not in the document's font_table is added to it automatically.
rtf_footnotes(<not an rtf_document>, ...) stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document object".
rtf_footnotes() before any content is added stops: "Cannot set footnotes before any content has been added.  Call rtf_footnotes() after rtf_tables() / rtf_figures(): ..."
rtf_footnotes(d, 1) stops: "`footnotes` must be a list (one block per page) or a character vector (one block for every page)."
rtf_footnotes() with a list of 3 blocks for 2 contents stops: "`footnotes` has 3 blocks but the document has 2 pages: give one block per page, or one block (a list of length 1) for every page."
rtf_footnotes(border = "top") stops: "`rtf_footnotes(border = )` must be NULL or an rtf_border() object."

A footnote row named other than l / c / r stops at render: "A footnote row may only be named l / c / r; got 'x'."; a per-row style list stops: "A footnote row is a string or a named vector such as c(l = "...", r = "..."). Per-row styling lists are no longer supported -- set the style on the block instead, via rtf_footnotes(font_size_half_points = , align = , ...)."

rtf_footnotes(align = "middle") stops: "`rtf_footnotes(align)` must be "left", "center" or "right"."; font_size_half_points and row_height_twips stop with the messages of rtf_titles(), named for rtf_footnotes().

rtf_watermark("DRAFT") returns an object of class rtf_watermark; with a document it writes one shape into each section's header group, behind the text, so it repeats on every page of the section and stays scoped to it.
rtf_watermark(text = ) is the watermark word; a zero-length or empty string means no watermark, and NA becomes the empty string.
rtf_watermark() with no text (or NULL, or character(0)) stops: "`text` is required; give the word to draw, e.g. "DRAFT"."
rtf_watermark(font_size_half_points = 144L) is the size in half-points (144 is 72 pt).
rtf_watermark("D", font_size_half_points = 0) stops: "`font_size_half_points` must be one positive number."
rtf_watermark(color = "#C8C8C8") is the fill colour as "#RRGGBB", written as the blue-green-red integer an Office shape property wants.
rtf_watermark("D", color = "red") (or NA) stops: "`color` must be one "#RRGGBB" string; got 'red'."
rtf_watermark(angle = -45) is the rotation in degrees, counter-clockwise negative, written as the fixed-point number (degrees times 65536) a shape wants; -45 is the bottom-left to top-right diagonal.
rtf_watermark("D", angle = "x") (or a vector) stops: "`angle` must be one number, in degrees."

rtf_watermark(font = ) is the font family; NULL (the default) uses the document font; a named vector per script slot is accepted, and the east_asian family is used when the text holds East Asian wide characters, the latin one otherwise.
rtf_watermark("X", font = c("A", "B")) stops: "`font` must be NULL or one font-family name."; a slot vector with an unknown slot stops: "`font`: unknown font slot(s) "bad"; use ...".
rtf_watermark(width_in = 6, height_in = 2) are the size in inches of the shape's bounding box.
rtf_watermark("D", width_in = -1) stops: "`width_in` must be one positive number, in inches."; likewise `height_in`.
rtf_header_source() returns one character string of source for an rtf_col_header(), name-based (cells written as column names, which survive reordering), keeping the header's empty gap cells.
rtf_header_source(x) takes an rtftable, or a list of rtftables (pages from as_rtftables()), the first page being used.
A non-syntactic column name is backtick-quoted in the source.
A table with no explicit header is written as its names(data) in one label row.

rtf_header_source(level = "explicit") writes only the fields that differ from the defaults; "default" also writes each cell's effective align and default border widths but not the FALSE decoration flags; "all" writes everything, bold = FALSE and the like included.
rtf_header_source(x, level = "x") stops: "'arg' should be one of "explicit", "default", "all"" (match.arg).
notes: match.arg message; no test

statement: rtf_header_source(snippet = TRUE), the default, wraps the header in a pipeable set_col_header(...) call (no leading tbl |>) that also reproduces the header text alignment and the header and spanning zone borders via style_zone(); snippet = FALSE returns the bare rtf_col_header(...) value.
rtf_header_source(add_span_level = TRUE) prepends a scaffold spanning row, the stub column(s) as single empty cells and every other column under one empty spanning cell; FALSE is the default.
rtf_header_source(stub = 1) names the column(s), by position or name, kept un-spanned when add_span_level = TRUE; the default is the first column.
The source rtf_header_source() writes, evaluated and given to set_col_header(), rebuilds the same header (a round trip).
rtf_header_source(1) (or a list that does not start with an rtftable, or an empty list) stops: "`rtf_header_source()` expects an rtftable or a list of rtftable pages (as returned by as_rtftables())."
rtf_header_source(add_span_level = TRUE, stub = "zz") (or a position outside the columns) stops: "`stub` must be valid column name(s) or position(s) in 1..2."

rtf_text_tokens() returns a data frame with the columns token (as written, with braces), kind ("page", "run" or "own"), when ("render", "viewer" or "assemble"), description and example, one row for each of {PAGE}, {TOTAL_PAGES}, {AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, {BOOK_PAGE}, {PROGRAM}, {PROGRAM_FULL}, {PROGRAM_NAME}, {PROGRAM_DIR} and {DATETIME}; every token listed is replaced when a file is written.

rtf_text_tokens(doc = rtf_document(tokens = list(...))) adds the document's tokens of one's own as rows of kind "own", with their value as the example, to the session's (options(rtfreporter.tokens = )); doc = NULL (the default) lists the session's only.
rtf_text_tokens("x") stops: "`doc` is an rtf_document (or NULL)."
For a token set both in options(rtfreporter.tokens = ) and in rtf_document(tokens = ), rtf_text_tokens(doc) lists it once with the document's value.
A page-value token written {<column name>} (from a table paginated on a column) is filled with the page's value, but rtfreporter's own tokens and a token of one's own of the same name win over it.
rtf_replace_text(input_file, target, replacement) replaces each target with its replacement in the file, in place, and returns the normalised path invisibly.
rtf_replace_text(input_file = ) is the path of the RTF file to read.

rtf_replace_text(target = c("DRAFT", "vX.Y"), replacement = c("FINAL", "v1.0")) replaces each target by the replacement at the same position; a single replacement is recycled to every target; the replacements are applied sequentially, so an earlier one can affect a later one.
rtf_replace_text(output_file = ) is the path the result is written to, leaving the input untouched; NULL (the default) overwrites input_file.
rtf_replace_text(backup = TRUE), the default, copies the original to paste0(input_file, ".bak") before overwriting in place; backup = FALSE makes no copy; it is ignored when output_file is given.
rtf_replace_text(use_regex = FALSE), the default, treats target as a fixed string, so regex metacharacters are literal; use_regex = TRUE treats it as a Perl-compatible regular expression.
rtf_replace_text(case_insensitive = TRUE) matches ignoring case; a fixed target is escaped first so its metacharacters stay literal; FALSE (the default) matches case-sensitively.
rtf_replace_text(encoding = "UTF-8") is the encoding of the input file, used when reading and writing.

rtf_replace_text() works on the file as plain text: a target matches only where it appears literally, so text split across RTF control words, or non-ASCII characters the renderer escaped, do not match their on-screen form.
rtf_replace_text(input_file = c("a", "b")) or a non-string stops: "`input_file` must be a single file path."
rtf_replace_text("no-such-file.rtf", "a", "b") stops: "`input_file` not found: no-such-file.rtf".
rtf_replace_text(input_file) without target or replacement stops: "Both `target` and `replacement` must be supplied."
rtf_replace_text(p, 1, "b") (target or replacement not character) stops: "`target` and `replacement` must be character vectors."
rtf_replace_text(p, character(0), "b") stops: "`target` is empty."
rtf_replace_text(p, c("a", "b"), c("1", "2", "3")) stops: "`replacement` must be the same length as `target`, or length 1."
rtfreporter_options() returns a named list with one element for every rtfreporter.* option, named by it, each the option's value where one is set and otherwise the factory baseline.

The factory baseline is: page letter, landscape, 0.75 inch margins; font "Courier New" at 18 half-points; markup "script"; title_format "text"; footnote_format "table"; figure.default_dpi 96; png_device "auto"; rounding "r"; and NULL for font_lang, row_height_twips, cell padding, title_width, footnote_width and ard_pipe.
An option set in the session (options(rtfreporter.font = "Arial")) appears in rtfreporter_options() in place of the factory value, the others staying at the factory baseline.
rtfreporter_reset_defaults() sets every rtfreporter.* option back to its factory value, e.g. rtfreporter.font to "Courier New" and rtfreporter.page.margin_top_in to 0.75, after they were changed.
rtfreporter_reset_defaults() returns invisibly the factory default list that was applied.
generate_rtfreport(doc, file_path) writes a valid, non-empty RTF file and returns file_path invisibly.
generate_rtfreport(doc = ) is an rtf_document from rtf_document() or an rtfreport object; report = is the superseded name of doc, documented and still working, by name or with the file by position.
generate_rtfreport(list(foo = 1), tempfile()) stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document (from rtf_document()) or rtfreport object."
generate_rtfreport(file_path = ) is the output RTF path; NULL (the default) is the document's own rtf_document(file = ), and one given here wins.
generate_rtfreport(doc) with no file_path and no rtf_document(file = ) stops: "generate_rtfreport(): no file to write -- give `file_path`, or the document's with `rtf_document(file = )`."
generate_rtfreport(doc, file_path = 1) stops: "`file_path` must be a single string: the RTF file's path."
generate_rtfreport(overwrite = TRUE), the default, writes over an existing file.
generate_rtfreport(doc, f, overwrite = FALSE) with f existing stops: "`file_path` already exists and `overwrite = FALSE`."

generate_rtfreport(program = "work/tfl/t_dm.R") overrides, for this one file, the program the document names, for {PROGRAM}, {PROGRAM_NAME} and {PROGRAM_DIR} (as given) and {PROGRAM_FULL} (made absolute from the working folder, with the system's separator); NULL (the default) uses the document's.
generate_rtfreport(program_fallback = ) overrides, for this one file, rtf_document(program_fallback = ): the program to name when none is said and none is found, said in a message when used.

When no program is said, the program is found, and said in a message: the file source() is running (the innermost), the script Rscript runs, the document knitr is knitting, the file open in RStudio's editor (interactive, not Untitled).

A program's file name is completed to the one on disk for every {PROGRAM...} token: a file that is there gets its real case; a name with no extension becomes the program of that name in its folder (.R, .r, .Rmd, .qmd), else gets .R; a name with an extension that is not there is kept.

A {PROGRAM}, {PROGRAM_FULL}, {PROGRAM_NAME} or {PROGRAM_DIR} token in a header, footer, title or footnote with no program known stops: "A header, footer, title or footnote uses {PROGRAM}, {PROGRAM_FULL}, {PROGRAM_NAME} or {PROGRAM_DIR}, but no program is known." followed by how to say one (rtf_document(program = ), source() or Rscript).

{DATETIME} is the time the file is written, as getOption("rtfreporter.datetime_format", "%d%b%Y  %H:%M") in the C locale (25Sep2026  10:05); {DATETIME:<format>} takes another strftime format; the time is taken once per file, so every page shows the same one, and options(rtfreporter.render_time = ) fixes it.
Run tokens are filled in titles and footnotes as well as in headers and footers.
Tokens of one's own ({STUDY}, {CUTOFF}) from rtf_document(tokens = ) and options(rtfreporter.tokens = ) are filled in headers, footers, titles and footnotes; a token not set is left as written.
A column header is not filled with tokens of one's own; it takes its values from set_col_header(values = ).

The page tokens are filled when the file is written: {PAGE} and {TOTAL_PAGES} as literal numbers (the section's first page, the file's total), {AUTO_PAGE} and {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES} as fields the word processor computes.

A {SECTION_PAGES} token stops: "`{SECTION_PAGES}` was removed: the RTF SECTIONPAGES field it wrote equals `{AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}` in a standalone file, ..." and names {TOTAL_PAGES} and {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES} to use.
rtf_columns(<rtftable>) returns the body column names, in order, as a character vector.
rtf_columns(<list of rtftables>), pages from as_rtftables(), returns the first page's columns; an empty list gives character(0).
rtf_columns(list("a")) stops: "`rtf_columns()` on a list expects rtftable pages (as returned by as_rtftables())."
rtf_col_header(...) returns a list of class "rtf_col_header" holding the rows in the order given, top row first.
A header row is a character vector with one label per data column.
A header row is a list of col_cell() objects, for a row of single and spanning cells.
A header row may be a named character vector, matched to the columns by name when the header meets its table; a single label is allowed.
rtf_col_header(c("a", "b"), c("A", "B", "C")) stops: "rtf_col_header(): the label rows must have one label per column, so the same length; rows 1, 2 have 2, 3 labels."
A table: the data frame as rtftable pages, its stub, column header, blank rows, widths, styles and borders, and the document it goes into.

as_rtftable() converts one table object (a gt_tbl, gtsummary table, rtables/tern table, rlistings listing, flextable, huxtable or data.frame/tibble) into a single rtftable, exactly as_rtftables(x, read_meta = read_meta, split = "none", ...)[[1]].

as_rtftables() turns a table object, or a list of them, into a list of rtftable pages: it reads the metadata the RTF renderer can use, then paginates the rendered body, replicating the header, widths and styles on every page.
rtf_tables() appends tables to a document, each element of tables being exactly one page with its title, footnote, section heading and placement.
stub_cols() merges the hierarchy columns of a tidy data frame into one indented stub column (or keeps them in place), with a label row for each parent value.
stub_spec() bundles the settings of stub_cols() into one rtf_stub_spec object for as_rtftables(stub = ).
set_col_header() replaces the whole column header of a finished rtftable, or of every page of a list, resolving each cell against the final printed columns by name or visible position.
add_col_header_row() appends or prepends one row to an rtf_col_header (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0).
add_header_row() adds one row to the column header of a finished rtftable, or of every page of a list, above or below the rows it has.
update_header_row() replaces or adds one row of an rtf_header() object (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0).
update_footer_row() replaces or adds one row of an rtf_footer() object (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0).
set_header_cell() places col_cell() cells into one row of the column header of a finished rtftable, keeping the other cells of that row (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0).
header_map() lists, one row per header cell of every page, the page, its keys, the columns the cell covers and its text.
col_header_from_names() builds a spanning rtf_col_header from delimited column names (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0).
add_cont_label() prepends a continuation row ("<label> (Cont.)") to a page chunk, for a custom split function of as_rtftables().
paginate() splits a table object into per-page data frames (deprecated in 0.8.x in favour of as_rtftables(), removed in 0.9.0).
paginate_cols() cuts built rtftable pages into column blocks, repeating the row-heading columns on each, with the header, widths and styles following the kept columns.
as_rtftable(x) returns one rtftable (not a list of pages), carrying the labels, alignment, spanning header, widths, title and footnote its source has, as as_rtftables(x, split = "none")[[1]] does.
as_rtftable(x = ) takes a gt_tbl, a gtsummary table, an rtables/tern VTableTree, an rlistings listing_df, a flextable, a huxtable, or a plain data.frame/tibble.
as_rtftable() accepts a gt_group (gt_group() / gt_split(), or a tfrmt page_plan render) or a gtsummary tbl_split holding exactly one table, and converts that table.
as_rtftable() on a gt_group of more than one table stops: "`x` is a gt_group holding 2 tables; use as_rtftables() to convert them all."
as_rtftable() on a gtsummary tbl_split of more than one table stops: "`x` is a tbl_split holding 2 tables; use as_rtftables() to convert them all."

as_rtftable() on anything that is not a table object stops: "`x` must be a gt_tbl, a gtsummary table, an rtables/tern table (VTableTree), an rlistings listing (listing_df), a flextable, a huxtable, or a data.frame/tibble."
as_rtftable(read_meta = ) is TRUE by default (read all render-relevant metadata), FALSE (rendered body only) or a character vector of tokens, as as_rtftables(read_meta = ) says.
as_rtftable(...) passes its further arguments to rtftable() (and on to as_rtftables()); an explicit value always wins over the value extracted from the source table.
as_rtftable(...) reaches the other settings of as_rtftables() (drop_cols, sort_by, collapse_repeats, listing, header_sep, stub) for the one page, so they act on it as they do there.
as_rtftable(gt_obj = ) is the old name of x: it still works and warns once a session, "`as_rtftable(gt_obj = )` is deprecated: the argument is `x` now. The old name is removed in 0.9.0."
as_rtftables(x) returns a list of rtftable objects, one per page; the list is named when the split is value-based or the input was a named list.

as_rtftables() is an S3 generic: a package that depends on rtfreporter makes its own class a source by registering as_rtftables.<class>(x, ...) returning rtftable pages, and rtf_tables() then accepts the object directly.
The title and source notes of the source travel with each page as the attributes rtf_titles and rtf_footnotes, which rtf_tables() consumes.

as_rtftables(x = ) takes a gt_tbl, gt_group, gtsummary table (or tbl_split), rtables/tern VTableTree, rlistings listing_df, flextable, huxtable, data.frame/tibble, or a list of these; the body is the rendered body (hidden and helper columns dropped, group rows interleaved, indentation in the label text).
A gt_group (and a tfrmt page_plan render) and a gtsummary tbl_split are expanded to one page set per member table, and an empty gt_group gives an empty list.

A list input is flattened in order: one input that makes one page keeps its name, one that makes several pages gives every page that name, and an input whose split already names its pages is named "<list name>.<page name>"; an empty list gives list().

as_rtftables() on an unsupported input stops: "`as_rtftables()` supports gt_tbl, gt_group, gtsummary, rtables/tern, rlistings, flextable, huxtable, data.frame/tibble, or a list of these; got '<class>'."

as_rtftables(read_meta = ) is TRUE by default (read all the metadata the source has), FALSE (the rendered body only) or a character vector of tokens naming the metadata read (for gt/gtsummary "col_header", "alignment", "spanning", "widths", "titles", "footnotes", "styles"; for rtables and rlistings also "indent" and "footnote_marks"; for a data.frame "labels").

For a data.frame or tibble, read_meta = "labels" (on by default) uses a column's label attribute as its header label (a column without one keeps its name), and tokens that are only meaningful to other adapters are ignored so a list mixing tables and data frames can share one read_meta.

as_rtftables(read_meta = ) that is not FALSE, TRUE or a character vector stops: "`read_meta` must be FALSE/TRUE or a character vector of tokens."; an unknown token stops: "Unknown <adapter> `read_meta` token(s): '<token>'.  Allowed: ...".

as_rtftables(split = ) is "none" by default (one page, no row limit checked); "rows" cuts before each position of split_rows; "group_safe" packs whole groups onto a page and splits a group that alone exceeds max_rows with a continuation label; "group_force" cuts every max_rows rows and repeats the group label on the next page; "by_value" makes one page per distinct value of group_col, named by it.

as_rtftables(split = <function>) takes a custom page-break rule called as split(df, max_rows =, group_col =, group_by =, cont_label =, min_group_rows =) on the cell-formatted body; it must return a non-empty list of data frames, one per page, and the names of the list become page names.
A custom split that returns anything but a non-empty list of data frames stops: "A custom `split` function must return a non-empty list of data.frames."
as_rtftables(max_rows = ) is the largest number of body rows on a page for split = "group_safe" and "group_force" (NULL by default), and is ignored by "none", "rows" and "by_value".

as_rtftables(split = "group_safe") or "group_force" without max_rows stops: "`max_rows` is required when split = \"group_safe\"." (likewise \"group_force\"); split = "rows" without split_rows stops: "`split_rows` is required when split = \"rows\"."
notes: the test of split_rows being required calls paginate() (test-paginate.R :: split = 'rows' requires split_rows), not as_rtftables()

statement: as_rtftables(split_rows = c(20, 40)), for split = "rows", cuts before those row positions and gives pages 1:19, 20:39, 40:nrow; it is ignored by the other splits.

as_rtftables(group_col = ) names, by column name or position, the column the group-aware splits ("group_safe", "group_force", "by_value") detect groups on; NULL (the default) uses column 1, and a factor group column is coerced to character before the split so the continuation label can be written into it.

as_rtftables(group_col = ) or collapse_repeats naming a column the table lacks stops: "`group_col` column 'nope' not found in the table." / "`group_col` index 9 out of range (1..2)." (likewise for `collapse_repeats`).

as_rtftables(group_by = ) is "auto" by default (leading indentation present: "indent"; else interspersed empty cells: "filled"; else "value"); "indent" starts a group at a non-empty group_col cell that does not begin with whitespace; "value" makes each maximal run of equal values a group; "filled" starts a group at each non-empty cell, NA and "" cells being members.
as_rtftables(group_by = ) or split = other than a listed value is refused by match.arg(), which names the allowed values.

as_rtftables(page_by = ) (NULL by default) cuts the body into one page per distinct value of the named column(s) first and names each page by the value (the pair, for two columns), and every other pagination setting then applies within one partition; a page gathers its rows even when the value is scattered, in the body's order.

A page cut with page_by is named by its outermost value alone; pages that share a heading are numbered with a "...n" tail ("Period 1...1", "Period 1...2"), a heading used once carries none, and the tail is not part of the heading auto_section and auto_title print; the page's rtf_paginate_meta holds page_group / page_by and page_values.
as_rtftables(page_by = "nope") on a column the body lacks stops: "`page_by` column 'nope' not found in the table."

as_rtftables(sort_by = ) (NULL by default, input order kept) orders the body rows before pagination by the named columns (names, positions, or a list mixing them) in the input body's coordinates; the sort is stable and NA keys sort last.
as_rtftables(sort_desc = ) is NULL/FALSE by default (all ascending), a single TRUE (all keys descending) or a logical vector with one direction per sort_by key; it is ignored when sort_by is NULL.

as_rtftables(sort_by = , sort_desc = ) misused stops: an unknown column, "`sort_by` column 'zz' not found in the table."; a position outside the body, "`sort_by` index 99 out of range (1..n)."; a sort_desc of the wrong length, "`sort_desc` must have length 1 or <n> (one per `sort_by`)."; a sort_desc with NA, "`sort_desc` must be TRUE / FALSE."
as_rtftables(cont_label = " (Cont.)") is the suffix appended to a group's label on the second and later pages a group continues onto, under "group_safe" and "group_force".
as_rtftables(min_group_rows = 2) moves the whole group to the next page when a page would end on a group that starts on it with fewer than that many child rows; 0 disables it.

as_rtftables(blank_rows = ) is NULL by default (no blanks, an rtf_blank_rows attribute already on the input still honoured) and takes integer positions (a blank after each given row, 0 before the first, -1 after the last), "between_groups" (a blank at each group transition of group_col under group_by), a blank_rows_by_change() or blank_rows_by_rule() object, or a list combining them.
A blank_rows entry that is none of the accepted forms stops: "Unrecognised `blank_rows` entry: ...".
notes: no test with as_rtftables() found for the stop() text

statement: as_rtftables(blank_row_first = , blank_row_end = ) (FALSE by default) add one blank row at the top, and at the bottom, of every page, after the split.

as_rtftables(count_blank_rows = TRUE) makes max_rows the number of rows the page prints (body rows, blank rows in the data, blanks from blank_rows, and the blank_row_first / blank_row_end edges, an edge merging with a blank row it sits against); FALSE, the default, counts only the rows of the input, so a page can print taller than max_rows.

as_rtftables(align_count_pct = ) is FALSE by default (no alignment); TRUE applies the built-in cell format "count_pct", realigning "n (xx.x)" cells to a uniform width; the name of a built-in cell format or a function behaves as cell_format; it is ignored when cell_format is given.

as_rtftables(align_count_pct = ) that is neither a switch, a built-in name nor a function stops: "`align_count_pct` must be TRUE / FALSE, the name of a built-in cell format, or a cell-format function."

as_rtftables(cell_format = ) (NULL by default) re-formats the body column by column before pagination: one formatter for every data column (the row-label column 1 is left alone), or a list taken positionally; a formatter is a function of a character column or the name of a built-in ("right_align", "count_paren", "count_paren_bare", "value_paren", "count_pct", the "fmt_" prefix optional).

as_rtftables(cell_format = ) misused stops: an unknown built-in, "`cell_format`: \"nope\" is not a built-in cell format.  The built-ins are ..."; a function returning a vector of another length, "A `cell_format` function must return a vector the same length as the column (got <n>, expected <m>)."

as_rtftables(na = "") is the text printed for a missing value, in every column including the row-label column and independently of align_count_pct / cell_format, which decide only whether the token is aligned with the counts; "" leaves the cell empty.

With as_rtftables(na = ), NaN counts as missing, while Inf and -Inf do not and print as "Inf" / "-Inf", the strings "NA" and "NaN" are never touched, and the NAs collapse_repeats writes per page stay blank.
as_rtftables(na = ) that is not a single non-NA string stops: "`na` must be a single string -- the text printed for a missing value (e.g. \"-\" or \"NA\").  \"\" (the default) leaves the cell empty."

as_rtftables(first_rows = ) (NULL by default) puts that many rows on the first page and paginates the rest as max_rows and split say, for the page a table shares with the content before it (rtf_tables(page_break = FALSE)).

as_rtftables(first_rows = ) with page_by or a custom split stops: "`first_rows` paginates one table by rows or groups: not with `page_by` or a custom `split`."; with split = "by_value" it stops: "`first_rows` paginates by rows or groups: not split = \"by_value\"."
notes: the by_value stop() text is not exercised by a test found

statement: as_rtftables(collapse_repeats = ) (NULL by default) names columns in priority order in which consecutive repeated values are blanked (NA) per page, after the split, keeping the first value of a run; with several columns each later column is collapsed on the combination of itself and the earlier ones.

as_rtftables(drop_cols = ) (NULL by default) hides the named columns (names, positions, or a list mixing them, in the input body's coordinates) from every printed page after pagination, so group_col, collapse_repeats and blank_rows_by_change() can still use them; col_spec, widths, col_header_align, row_title and cell_styles are reindexed to the remaining columns.

as_rtftables(drop_cols = ) naming every column stops: "`drop_cols` must leave at least one column to display."; an unknown name or a position out of range stops: "`drop_cols` column 'nope' not found in the table." / "`drop_cols` index 99 out of range (1..n)."

as_rtftables(listing = ) (a listing_spec() object, NULL by default) applies to a data.frame/tibble: build_listing() reshapes it into a listing body (joined columns, wrapped cells, gutters, a blank row after each record) and the spec supplies the col_header, relative widths and left alignment.
A body already built by build_listing() carries its own spec, which as_rtftables() picks up.

as_rtftables(listing = ) on an rlistings listing_df stops: "`listing` does not apply to an rlistings listing (`listing_df`): rlistings has already laid it out.  Drop `listing` and pass it to `as_rtftables()` as it is."; on a source that is not a data frame it stops: "`listing` applies to a data.frame or tibble source; got '<class>'."; a value that is not a listing_spec() stops: "`listing` must be a listing_spec(); got '<class>'."; on a body already built by build_listing() it stops: "`data` was already built by build_listing(), and carries its own listing spec.  Drop the `listing` argument, or pass the unbuilt source data."
notes: the rlistings and not-a-data-frame messages are not matched by a test found

statement: as_rtftables(stub = ) (NULL by default, no stub) takes a stub_spec() object or, as shorthand for stub_spec(vars), a bare vector of hierarchy columns, and applies stub_cols() to the extracted body before pagination.

as_rtftables(stub_vars = , stub_label = , stub_indent = , stub_group_summary = ) are deprecated: they warn once a session ("`stub_vars` / `stub_label` / `stub_indent` / `stub_group_summary` are deprecated: write `stub = stub_spec(vars, label = , indent = , group_summary = )` (or `stub = vars`).") and still build the same stub as stub = stub_spec().
notes: Section help of stub_spec() says the stub_vars family is superseded and "not deprecated", while as_rtftables() help and the code say deprecated and warn

statement: as_rtftables() given both stub and any of stub_vars, stub_label, stub_indent or stub_group_summary stops: "Pass either `stub` or the superseded `stub_vars` family, not both."

The stub is built on the extracted body before pagination, so drop_cols, group_col, sort_by, group_by = "indent" and the group-aware splits refer to the reshaped body; a source that already renders an indented stub (rtables/tern, tfrmt indented, gtsummary) is not given another.

as_rtftables(header_sep = ) is the separator(s) used to rebuild a spanning, multi-row header from a plain data.frame's column names: each name is split into segments that become stacked header rows, adjacent columns sharing a label and ancestor path become one spanning cell, a name with no separator keeps its name on the leaf row, and a doubled "____" gives a blank cell at that level; the default is both "____" and "___tlang_delim___", NULL disables it.

as_rtftables(auto_width = TRUE) sizes each column to its widest content (header label or data cell) via auto_col_widths() and decides how the columns divide the table, not how wide the table is; FALSE is the default.
as_rtftables(table_width_twips = ) is the table's total width in twips (NULL by default), as rtftable(table_width_twips = ) means it, independent of auto_width.
as_rtftables(border = "tfl", style = NULL) are passed to rtftable() for every page; the default border is the "tfl" preset.

as_rtftables(...) forwards further arguments (col_header, col_spec, row_title, col_rel_width, column_widths_twips, row_height_twips, cell_styles, ...) to rtftable() for every page, an explicit value winning over one extracted from the source; a user col_header is resolved against the final printed columns, after stub and drop_cols.
Explicit cell_styles of the caller with one element per body row follow their rows through the stub, the sort and the page split instead of being handed whole to every page.
rtf_tables(doc, tables) appends the tables as pages of the document and returns the modified rtf_document; each element of tables becomes exactly one page.
rtf_tables() with a doc that is not an rtf_document stops: "`doc` must be an rtf_document object".

rtf_tables(tables = ) takes a table_plan (its pages as plan_apply() makes them), the output of as_rtftables(), a bare data.frame (one simple page with rtftable() defaults), an rtftable, an rtfplot, a gt_tbl or gtsummary table, a list of these, or an object of a class with a registered as_rtftables() method.
notes: no test found for a table_plan passed as tables

statement: rtf_tables() with a list element that is not a page content stops: "Item 2 is a 'character'. Each list element is one page: a data.frame, rtftable(), rtfplot(), gt_tbl or gtsummary table. ..." naming where other tables go (as_rtftables()); an element that is itself a list of contents is refused the same way.

rtf_tables(titles = ) is NULL by default, or a list of length(tables) title blocks, or of length 1 (one block for every page); a block is a character vector (one entry per row) or a list of rows, each a string or a styled list(text, align, bold, italic, underline, color, border); "" is a blank row, and rows default to centred and bold.

rtf_tables(footnotes = ) is NULL by default, or a list of length(tables) or length 1 blocks of the same form as titles; footnote rows default to left-aligned and the first row carries a top rule unless it sets its own border.
Where titles or footnotes are NULL for a page, rtf_tables() uses the rtf_titles / rtf_footnotes attributes the page carries (as as_rtftables() sets them from the source).

rtf_tables(titles = , footnotes = ) of the wrong shape stops: "`titles` must be a list (or NULL)."; a list of the wrong length stops: "`titles` has 2 blocks but there is 1 page: give one block per page, or one block (a list of length 1) for every page."
Title and footnote text may carry the page-number tokens {AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, {PAGE} and {TOTAL_PAGES}, and a table paginated on a column fills {<column name>} with its page's value.

rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) on a named tables list opens a section at each page name that changes, with the name as the heading appended to the common header of rtf_section(secinfo = ); a run of pages with the same name is one section, an empty name continues the open section, and a "...n" tail is stripped. NULL, the default, takes what the pages say, else FALSE.
rtf_tables(section_label_align = "left") sets the alignment of the auto-appended section label row; "center" and "right" are the other values.
notes: the argument is passed through without a check in rtf_tables(); no test of the alignment itself found

statement: rtf_tables(auto_title = TRUE) on a named tables list appends each page name as the last row of that table's title block (the name alone when the table has no title), leaving unnamed items untouched; NULL, the default, takes what the pages say, else FALSE.
rtf_tables(title_label_align = "left") sets the alignment of the auto_title label row ("left", "center" or "right").
rtf_tables(auto_title = TRUE, title_label_align = "up") stops: "`title_label_align` must be \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"."

rtf_tables(page_break = TRUE) (the default) begins each table on a new page; FALSE puts a table under the content before it, on the page that one ends on, with nothing measured; one value for every table or one each; a table's own later pages and the document's first content always begin a page.
rtf_tables(page_break = ) that is not TRUE or FALSE, or not of length 1 or the number of pages, stops: "rtf_tables(): `page_break` is TRUE or FALSE, one for every page or one each (<n>)."

rtf_tables(first_rows = ) (NULL by default) with page_break = FALSE puts that many rows of the one table on the shared page and paginates the rest as the table says, each page with its title, column header and footnote; tables is then a table_plan, a data frame or an rtftable.

rtf_tables(first_rows = ) misused stops: without page_break = FALSE, "rtf_tables(): `first_rows` is the rows a table puts on the page before it: page_break = FALSE."; not a whole number of 1 or more, "rtf_tables(): `first_rows` is a whole number of rows, 1 or more."; with pages already built, "rtf_tables(): `first_rows` takes one table -- a table_plan, a data frame or an rtftable; pages already built take it where they are built: as_rtftables(first_rows = )."
rtf_tables(space_before = 0) with page_break = FALSE puts that many empty lines between the content before and this table (0 leaves the title's own blank line alone).
rtf_tables(space_before = -1) (or a value that is not a single whole number of 0 or more) stops: "rtf_tables(): `space_before` is a whole number of empty lines, 0 or more."

rtf_tables(cont_title = ) (NULL by default, none) is a line under the title of each later page of a table, for the pages after the shared one of first_rows and for a table's own later pages (a plan's, or as_rtftables()'s max_rows pages).
rtf_tables(cont_title = 1) (anything but one string or NULL) stops: "rtf_tables(): `cont_title` is one line of text, or NULL."

rtf_tables(col_header, col_header_align, spanning_header, col_spec, row_title, border, blank_rows, read_attributes, style, col_rel_width, column_widths_twips, table_width_twips, table_width_pct_of_writable, table_width_pct, table_align, row_height_twips, row_height_exact, header_row_height_twips, blank_row_height_twips, cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips, cell_valign, blank_row_normalize, markup, font_size_half_points, font) are the table-format arguments of rtftable(), deprecated: each one passed says once a session, "`rtf_tables(<arg> = )` is deprecated: write a table's appearance in rtftable(), as_rtftables() or plan_style() (a bare data.frame takes their defaults). Removed in 0.9.0.", and still applies.

A deprecated table-format argument passed explicitly builds a bare data.frame element and overrides the matching field of a pre-built rtftable page, which otherwise keeps its own and its gt-derived settings; rtfplot pages are never modified.

rtf_tables(read_gt = ) is deprecated (removed in 0.9.0): passed, it says once a session to pass a gt or gtsummary table through as_rtftables(), and still reads the table's labels, alignment, titles and source notes.

stub_cols(data, vars) merges the hierarchy columns vars (parent first, leaf last) into one stub column placed first: each parent value becomes a label row (the other columns NA, rendering empty) and the leaf rows below it are indented with non-breaking spaces; the other columns follow in their original order.
stub_cols(vars = ) is a character or integer vector, or a list mixing names and positions, of the columns to merge; one column is the stub as it is, named label, with every row its own.

A label row is emitted at every run of a parent value, not once per distinct value, and a change in a higher-level column starts a new run in every column below it; with more than two vars each level indents one step further.
An NA or empty parent cell contributes no label row and no indentation for its rows, which keeps a summary row (such as "Subjects with at least one adverse event") flush left.
stub_cols(label = NULL) names the merged stub column; NULL joins the display names of the merged columns with " / " (a column's label attribute when it has one).
stub_cols(indent = 4L) is the number of non-breaking spaces prepended per nesting level; 0 leaves the leaf unpadded.

stub_cols(group_summary = c("empty", "parent")) names which leaf values mark a row as its group's summary: "empty" an NA or "" leaf, "parent" a leaf equal to its deepest non-empty parent; "all" is both and "none" or NULL disables; such a row's statistics are placed on the group's label row and no separate leaf row is emitted.

stub_cols(layout = "merged") (the default) replaces the hierarchy columns by one indented stub column; layout = "columns" keeps them in their original positions and with their own headers, a group value moving onto its own row, blank on the member rows, whose leaf is indented in the leaf column.

stub_cols(label_span = TRUE) (FALSE by default) renders each group label row as one cell spanning the table, recorded as attr(out, "rtf_label_rows") that rtftable(read_attributes = TRUE) consumes; a group-summary row folded onto a label row is never spanned.

Column label attributes on the columns that remain are preserved, so as_rtftables() can still pick them up as header labels; a zero-row data frame gives a zero-row stub layout; the result carries attr(out, "rtf_stub_src"), the source row of each output row (NA for an inserted label row).

stub_cols() misused stops: data that is not a data frame, "`data` must be a data.frame."; vars naming no column, "`vars` names no column."; a column twice, "`vars` must name distinct columns."; an unknown column, "`vars` column 'nope' not found in the table."; a position outside the data, "`vars` index 9 out of range (1..n)."

stub_cols() with a label that is not NULL or one string stops: "`label` must be NULL or a single string."; an indent that is not one non-negative integer, "`indent` must be a single non-negative integer."; a label_span that is not TRUE or FALSE, "`label_span` must be TRUE or FALSE."; a group_summary token other than "empty", "parent", "all", "none", "`group_summary` must be a subset of c(\"empty\", \"parent\") (or \"all\" / \"none\" / NULL); got: ...".

stub_cols(layout = "columns") with label_span = TRUE stops: "`label_span` applies to layout = \"merged\" only; with layout = \"columns\" the group value stays in its own column."; with a label it stops: "`label` names the merged stub column, which layout = \"columns\" does not create."; an unknown layout is refused by match.arg().
stub_cols() reads the values of the hierarchy columns as character, an NA as empty, whatever their type.
stub_spec(vars, label, indent, group_summary, layout, label_span) returns an rtf_stub_spec object carrying every stub_cols() setting, for as_rtftables(stub = ).
stub_spec() takes stub_cols()'s defaults: label NULL, indent 4, group_summary c("empty", "parent"), layout "merged", label_span FALSE.
stub_spec() without vars (missing or NULL) stops: "`vars` is required: the hierarchy columns, parent first."
stub_spec(layout = "nope") is refused at construction by match.arg(); the other settings are checked when stub_cols() builds the stub.
print() of an rtf_stub_spec shows the vars, layout and indent, and the label and label_span lines when set.

set_col_header(x, ...) replaces the whole column header of a finished rtftable and returns the table; every cell is resolved against the final printed columns, by name or by visible position (1 is the first printed column), whatever drop_cols or a stub did before.

set_col_header(...) are the header rows, top first: a character vector (a label row), a list of col_cell() cells (a spanning row) or one prebuilt rtf_col_header(); one argument is a whole header in any of those shapes and several are consecutive rows.
set_col_header(x) with no rows clears the header, so the column names print as the header.

A label row whose entries are all named is a patch: each label goes to the column of that name, the row may be shorter than the table, and the columns it does not mention keep their own name; an unnamed row gives one label per printed column, and an unnamed value that is itself a column name goes to that column.
notes: help text of set_col_header() says a row that is only partly named is an error; the code accepts a partly named row (an unnamed value is matched as a column name, else placed by position)

statement: A col_cell() pos may be column names or final positions, a column range c(a, b), or a selector such as col_key(); a selector that matches no column or non-adjacent columns is an error.

set_col_header() with an unnamed label row of the wrong length stops: "`set_col_header`: the label row has 2 labels but the table has 3 printed columns. ..." (a header written for the whole table does not fit pages that kept some columns).

set_col_header() naming a column the table lacks stops: for a col_cell(), "`pos` column name \"zzz\" not found in data columns. Available: ..."; for a named label row, "col_header: unknown column name \"zzz\". Available: ..."; two entries for one column stop: "col_header: column 2 (\"b\") is targeted twice -- ...".
set_col_header() given a header row that is a list but not made of col_cell() cells stops, saying it is not a cell and that cells go in list(), not c().

set_col_header(align = ) (NULL by default, header alignment left as it is) sets the header text alignment of the final columns: "left", "center" or "right" for every column, or a character vector with one value per printed column.

set_col_header(align = ) of the wrong length stops: "`set_col_header(align = )` must have length 1 or 3 (one per printed column)."; a value other than left, center or right stops: "`set_col_header(align = )` values must be \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"."

set_col_header(values = ) is a data frame with one row per page key and one column per {token}: the header is written once with {name} where a value belongs and each page takes the row its key matches; {{ is a literal brace, and the render-time tokens ({PAGE}, {TOTAL_PAGES}, {BOOK_PAGE}, {AUTO_PAGE}, {AUTO_TOTAL_PAGES}, {PROGRAM}, {PROGRAM_FULL}, {DATETIME}, ...) are left for the renderer.

set_col_header(by = ) says which page key the key columns of values are matched on: "group" (the default; the value a split = "by_value" page was cut for, else the page name without its "...n" tail), "rows" (the page_by value) or "name" (the page's name, "...n" included, always unique); several may be given to match on the combination.

set_col_header(values = ) with by = "group" on pages that have no group axis matches on the page name and says so once, as a message: "set_col_header(values = ): no group axis, so `by = \"group\"` matches on the page name instead."

set_col_header(values = ) misused stops: values that is not a data frame, "`values` must be a data.frame: one row per page key, one column per token."; a missing key column, "`values` has no key column `group`.  Name the key column after the axis it matches: `group`, `rows`, `name`."; a by that is not a page axis, "`by`: \"bogus\" is not a page axis (group, rows, name)."

set_col_header(values = ) that does not match the pages stops: a page with no row, "`values` has no row for page <i> (<name>). looked for <by> = \"<key>\" values has: ..."; a row no page used, "`values` row <i> matched no page: ... Every row must be used -- a row left over is usually a label that does not match the data."; a token with no value, "<where>: no value for `{token}`. Supply it in `values`, or write `{{` for a literal brace. values has: ...".
set_col_header() on a list maps over every page of an as_rtftables() list and returns a list of the same names; a table of several data frames (multi-DF mode) takes one header for each.
add_col_header_row(hdr, row) returns a new rtf_col_header with row appended below the existing rows; any value that rtftable(col_header = ) accepts as hdr is promoted to an rtf_col_header first.
add_col_header_row(.position = ) is "bottom" (the default) to append below the existing rows or "top" to prepend above them; row is a character vector or a list of cell specs.
notes: The default here is "bottom", while add_header_row() defaults to "top"

statement: add_col_header_row() is deprecated: it warns once a session, "`add_col_header_row()` is deprecated: write the row in `rtf_col_header()` itself (its rows, top first). Removed in 0.9.0.", and still does its job.

add_header_row(x, row) adds one row to the column header of a finished rtftable (or of every page of a list) and returns it; the row is normalised against the final printed columns as set_col_header() does.
add_header_row(row) is a character vector (a label row, optionally named to place labels by column name) or a list of col_cell() cells (a spanning row).
add_header_row(.position = ) is "top" (the default) to put the new row above the existing header rows, or "bottom" to put it below.
add_header_row() on a table with no column header takes the column names as the header, so the new row goes above or below them and does not replace them.

add_header_row(positon = ) (an argument the method does not have) warns and ignores it: "`add_header_row()`: unknown argument `positon` (did you mean `.position`?) ignored. Valid arguments: row, .position."

add_header_row() with an unnamed label row of the wrong number of labels stops: "`col_header` row 1 has <n> labels but the table has <m> columns.  Give one label per column, or name the ones to change: c(<column> = \"...\")."; .position other than top or bottom is refused by match.arg().
notes: no test of add_header_row() itself with a wrong-length row found

statement: update_header_row(header, row, content) replaces row `row` of an rtf_header() object with content (a named character vector, e.g. c(l = "Left", r = "Right")) and returns the modified header.
update_header_row() with a row beyond the current number of rows fills the rows in between with empty centre rows c(c = "") and puts content at row `row`.
The names of a character content are preserved, so the cell positions (l, c, r) it names survive.

update_header_row() with a first argument that is not an rtf_header() or rtf_footer() object stops: "First argument must be an rtf_header() or rtf_footer() object."; a row below 1 stops: "`row` must be >= 1."

update_header_row() is deprecated: it warns once a session, "`update_header_row()` is deprecated: make the header again with `rtf_header(rows = )` (a list of rows). Removed in 0.9.0.", and still does its job.

update_footer_row(footer, row, content) replaces row `row` of an rtf_footer() object with content, or appends it with empty centre rows c(c = "") filling any gap, exactly as update_header_row() does for a header.

update_footer_row() with a first argument that is not an rtf_header() or rtf_footer() object stops: "First argument must be an rtf_header() or rtf_footer() object."; a row below 1 stops: "`row` must be >= 1."

update_footer_row() is deprecated: it warns once a session, "`update_footer_row()` is deprecated: make the footer again with `rtf_footer(rows = )` (a list of rows). Removed in 0.9.0.", and still does its job.

set_header_cell(x, ..., row) places the col_cell() cells into header row `row` (1 is the top) of a finished rtftable, keeping the cells of that row they do not replace; merging separate cells into one spanning cell replaces their individual labels with the span label.

set_header_cell(...) are col_cell() objects whose pos may be column names or positions (a span as c(a, b)), resolved against the final columns; their align, border, bold, italic and underline are applied to the cell; a label row is promoted to cells first.
set_header_cell(row = ) is the single existing header row to edit, required; a new row is added with add_header_row().

set_header_cell() misused stops: no cell, "Provide at least one col_cell() to place."; row missing, "`row` (a single header-row index, 1 = top) is required."; a table with no header, "This rtftable has no column header; use set_col_header() first."; row out of range, "`row` must be in 1..<n> (the header rows, top first). To add a new row use add_header_row()."; an argument that is not a col_cell(), "`set_header_cell()` takes col_cell() objects in `...`."

set_header_cell() with cells that overlap one another stops: "Requested header cells overlap (columns 1-2 and 2-3)."; with a target that would split an existing spanning cell it stops: "Target columns 4-5 do not align to existing header-cell boundaries in that row (would split a spanning cell); adjust the span."; a cell outside the table stops: "col_cell() covers columns <a>-<b>, outside 1..<n>."

set_header_cell() on a list maps over every page; it is deprecated, warning once a session, "`set_header_cell()` is deprecated: write the spanning cell in the header (`rtf_col_header()` / `set_col_header()`, a new row with `add_header_row()`) and restyle cells with `style_header()`. Removed in 0.9.0.", and still does its job.

header_map(x) returns a data frame with one row per header cell of every page and the columns page, name, group, rows, row (which header row), cell, from, to and text; a label-row cell covers one column (from = to), a spanning cell from..to.
header_map(x = ) is an rtftable or a list of them (pages from as_rtftables()).
header_map() gives group as the page's group key (else its name without the "...n" tail) and rows as its page_by value (NA when it has none), the keys set_col_header(values = ) matches on.
header_map() on a page with no column header contributes no row, and on tables with none returns a zero-row data frame with the same columns.

col_header_from_names(names) returns an rtf_col_header: names split on the separator become stacked rows, adjacent columns with the same label and ancestor path merge into one spanning cell, and a name with no separator is bottom-aligned with blank cells above.
col_header_from_names(names = ) is a character vector or a data frame (its names are used); when no name splits into more than one segment the result is one flat label row of the names.

col_header_from_names(sep = ) is the separator(s) to split names on, the longest matching one winning; the default recognises "____" and "___tlang_delim___", and a doubled separator gives a blank cell at that level.
col_header_from_names() with no names stops: "`names` must be a non-empty character vector (or a data.frame)."

col_header_from_names() is deprecated: it warns once a session, "`col_header_from_names()` is deprecated: `as_rtftables()` builds this header from a data.frame's names (`header_sep =`), and a plan from its column keys. Removed in 0.9.0.", and still does its job.
add_cont_label(data, label) returns data with one row prepended: paste0(label, cont_label) in column col and every other cell empty ("" for a character column, NA otherwise); the row names are reset.

add_cont_label(cont_label = " (Cont.)") is the suffix appended to label, matching the built-in group strategies; add_cont_label(col = 1L) is the column, by name or position, where the label is placed.
add_cont_label() coerces a factor label column (the whole column) to character first, so it can hold the suffixed label.

add_cont_label() misused stops: data that is not a data frame, "`data` must be a data.frame."; a label that is not one string, "`label` must be a single string."; a col that is not there, "`col` 'x' not found in `data`." or "`col` index 9 out of range (1..n)."
add_cont_label(chunk = ) is the old name of data: it still works and warns once a session, "`add_cont_label(chunk = )` is deprecated: the argument is `data` now. The old name is removed in 0.9.0."
paginate() is deprecated: it warns once a session, pointing to as_rtftables(), and still returns a list of data frames, one per page, for rtf_tables().

paginate(x) takes a gt_tbl (its rendered body), a data.frame or tibble (the class kept on every page), or a list of these (flattened, a named input keeping or repeating its name per page, "<name>.<page>" when the split names its pages); an empty list gives list().

paginate(...) takes the pagination controls shared with as_rtftables(): max_rows, split ("none", "rows", "group_safe", "group_force", "by_value"), split_rows, group_col, cont_label, blank_rows, blank_row_first, blank_row_end, align_count_pct and na.

Every page returned by paginate() carries the attributes rtf_blank_rows (blank-row positions, which rtftable(read_attributes = TRUE) consumes) and rtf_paginate_meta (strategy, group_col, page_index, total_pages, page_name).
paginate() on any other class stops: "paginate() has no method for class '<class>'. Supported types: gt_tbl, data.frame / tibble, list of either."

paginate(split = "rows") without split_rows stops: "`split_rows` is required when split = \"rows\"."; "group_safe" or "group_force" without max_rows stops: "`max_rows` is required when split = \"group_safe\"."; a group_col not in the table stops: "`group_col` 'x' not found in the table."

paginate_cols(x, ...) cuts built rtftable pages into column blocks and returns a list of rtftable pages, the row-heading columns repeated on every block and the header, widths, col_spec, cell_styles, row_title and blank rows following the kept columns.

paginate_cols(x = ) is an rtftable or a list of rtftable pages that all have the same columns (a multi-DF table is cut on every constituent frame); positions refer to the final printed columns, after drop_cols, stub and a user col_header; an empty list gives an empty list.
paginate_cols(at = ) names, by name or position, the columns to cut before: at = c(4, 6) gives the blocks 1:3, 4:5 and 6:ncol.

paginate_cols(cut_by = ) says where to cut other than by position, as plan_paginate_cols() says it: a list of column blocks, or a separator found in the column names, or one key per column (each run of one key is a block); cols and by are the superseded spellings of the same two forms.
paginate_cols(every = ) cuts a block every that many columns, counting only the columns a block does not keep; a table no wider than one block is returned as it is.

paginate_cols(keep = ) is the row-heading columns every block repeats (carry is the superseded spelling), by default the table's row_title (column 1 unless set); keep = integer(0) repeats nothing, and a kept column is removed from the blocks so it is never printed twice.

paginate_cols(fit = TRUE) (width = "fill", the default) fixes the twips per ratio unit on page 1 and reuses it on every block, so page 1 fills the sheet and a given ratio is the same width throughout; fit = FALSE (width = "keep") gives each kept column the width it had before the split; absolute column_widths_twips are carried through verbatim and ignore both.

paginate_cols() with fit = TRUE (width = "fill") on a block totalling more ratio than block 1 warns: "`paginate_cols()`: column block 2 totals more than block 1, so its page is wider than the sheet. Put the widest block first, or use width = \"keep\"."

paginate_cols(order = ) (page_order is the superseded spelling) is the order the pages come out in, the axes outermost first from "group", "rows" and "cols" (axes left out are appended in that order), or "across" (group, cols, rows; the default) or "down" (group, rows, cols); the pages are the same whatever the order.

paginate_cols() returns the pages with the names they had, each column page keeping its row page's name, repeated names numbered with a "...n" tail so the list stays addressable by name; an unnamed list stays unnamed.

paginate_cols(col_header = ) is the header each page should carry, written once in the full table's coordinates (a label row or rows of col_cell()) and sliced to each page's columns with spanning cells clipped; "names" builds the two-level header the column names carry (the by key above, the rest below, a kept column under no spanning cell); NULL (the default) slices the table's own header.
paginate_cols(allow_span_break = TRUE) lets a cut fall inside a spanning header cell, the group's label being repeated over its remaining columns on each page; FALSE rejects such a cut.

paginate_cols() with no way to cut stops: "One of `at` (the columns to cut before), `cols` or `by` is required."; with two ways it stops: "Give one of `at`, `cols` or `by`, not at and cols." (or "`paginate_cols()`: say where to cut one way -- `at`, `cut_by` or `every`."); a new and an old spelling together stop: "`paginate_cols()`: give `cut_by` or the older `cols`, not both."
